title: Advanced Imaging of the Lumbar Spine (fictional)

chunks.text: Diagnosis must be consistent with lumbar radiculopathy or persistent low back pain (ICD-10 M54.16, M54.5x, or equivalent).
At least 6 weeks of documented conservative therapy is required: physical therapy, NSAIDs, and/or activity modification, unless a red-flag exception in §4 applies.
Objective neurologic deficit or persistent radicular symptoms must be documented (e.g., positive SLR, reflex change, dermatomal numbness, motor weakness).
No lumbar MRI in the prior 12 months without documented interval clinical change.
Red-flag exceptions waive the 6-week conservative-therapy requirement: suspected cauda equina, malignancy, infection, or fracture.
Documentation should include PT discharge summary or visit notes when available to strengthen the audit trail.

guidelines.text: ACR Appropriateness Criteria: MRI usually appropriate for subacute radiculopathy after conservative care.
ACR: imaging usually not appropriate in first 6 weeks of uncomplicated low back pain without red flags.
ACR: emergent imaging indicated for cauda equina symptoms (saddle anesthesia, urinary retention).
ACP 2017: clinicians should not routinely obtain imaging in patients with nonspecific low back pain.
ACP 2017: continue conservative therapy and reassess; imaging if progressive neurologic findings.
ACP 2017: imaging appropriate when patient is a candidate for intervention after failed conservative care.
NASS: suspected cauda equina requires urgent MRI and surgical evaluation.
NASS: radiculopathy with objective deficit after conservative care supports advanced imaging.
CMS-0057-F: urgent prior auth decisions within 72 hours; standard within 7 calendar days (from 2026).
